title: termal_review_freeze_check refuses a relative manifestPath in a linked worktree
outcome: termal_review_freeze_check resolves a relative manifestPath such as .git/engram-review-freeze.json correctly in a linked worktree, where .git is a file pointing to the worktree's Git dir, or refuses it with a message naming the absolute gitdir path to use. The documented relative example works, or the docs say it doesn't in linked worktrees.
acceptance: In a linked worktree whose .git is a file, a relative manifestPath whose first component is ".git" resolves under that worktree's own Git dir, so ".git/engram-review-freeze.json" finds a manifest written there, for both termal_review_freeze_check and the compiled review-freeze-check command.
A test that creates a real linked worktree, writes the manifest in its own Git dir and checks it by the relative path passes; it fails on the unfixed code (RED first).

Absolute paths, relative paths in a main checkout, and the existing escape refusals (e.g. "../outside.json", paths outside the root and own Git dir) behave exactly as before, shown by the existing tests passing unchanged.
The freeze documentation states that the relative ".git/..." form works in linked worktrees.
